scope: Abliterated main-model checkpoints for one DGX Spark. Published research only; these additional discoveries have not been downloaded, run, or promoted by this review.
exclusions: Tensor-parallel main models requiring two or more Sparks
Apple or RTX-only throughput presented as DGX Spark throughput

priority.priority: First additional Flash-Next recipe to qualify
priority.recipe: T3: pinned B12X vLLM, native MTP2, reduced 98,304-token draft vocabulary, FP8 KV and decode projection copies, disk-backed PLE, one Spark.

published.method: Medians of three suites; separate serial prose/code and aggregate concurrency results.
published.pin_note: Recipe files were added after the checkpoint pin; fetch the recipe revision separately from the weights.

evidence_checked: Portable launcher and pinned Docker arguments
limitations: FP8 projection copies change the numerical target; a greedy audit against that same target does not prove equality to the original model.
Eight-slot headroom and actual app coexistence need local measurement.
Large pinned patch surface increases maintenance work; do not treat this as unmodified upstream vLLM.
Published benchmark is not a Hermes deployment qualification.

local_trial.note: Read manual review: original score misses strict JSON and extra stop-dispatch issues. Different engines and caching; no broad quality claim.

priority.priority: Strong agent-specific challenger, with explicit behavior concerns
priority.recipe: Abliterated Flash-Next MLX-format 4-bit weights served by TensorFold CUDA 0.5.0 on one Spark, MTP and file-backed PLE.
evidence_checked: Model card distinguishes actual TensorFold CUDA measurement from autogenerated MLX usage snippets.
Real Hermes system prompt and tool-loop evaluation reported.
limitations: Some action-caution scenarios failed; scores do not establish safe autonomous fleet operation.
Vision unavailable on tested CUDA runtime.
Some latency tests used a local shared-prefix patch.
TensorFold 0.6.x changes outputs/cache behavior; these 0.5.0 results cannot be carried forward.

local_trial.note: Read manual review: original score misses strict JSON and extra stop-dispatch issues. Different engines and caching; no broad quality claim.

priority.priority: Promising EXL3 alternative, lower reproducibility confidence
priority.recipe: Huihui abliterated Flash-Next requant, integer-pinned EXL3 3.05bpw, MTP2 plus n-gram speculation k7.
evidence_checked: refusal_bench.py sends six requests sequentially (three mixed prose/code prompts repeated twice), temperature .5, thinking off, max 400 tokens.
Rate is completion tokens divided by whole-request elapsed time; reported median code selects upper-middle sample, not the mean of two central samples.
Five is configured concurrency capacity, not five simultaneous speed requests in the published script.
validation_battery.py checks tool-call emission; it does not implement the second tool-result turn despite its round-trip label.
limitations: No raw speed receipts or explicit warmup exclusion in published repository.
Author's two servers are independent one-Spark instances; no two-Spark requirement.
Broad quality and quantization loss not established.
Precise serving-engine pin and full launch recipe need resolution before a reproducible trial.

priority.priority: Strong smaller-model recipe to compare if the current Huihui lane disappoints
priority.recipe: Abliterated OrcaRouter parent, ModelOpt mixed NVFP4/FP8 MSE export, SGLang, calibrated DFlash2 depth8, BF16 KV and Mamba.

published.method: C1, thinking off, greedy, fixed128 output, one warmup plus seven measured requests.

limitations: Parent/base benchmark sample IDs and prompts were not available: published deltas are not a matched comparison.
No local Hermes result for this checkpoint.
Speed gain combines target quantization and draft changes; it is not a pure checkpoint effect.

other_leads.why: Same checkpoint as the current trial, different SGLang overlay, unquantized DFlash2 depth8 and FP8 KV; published 57.95 whole-request tok/s versus12.31 without speculation.
other_leads.limits: Headline pools18 performance requests: prose21.55, code66.82, math52.30, reasoning43.23, copy Python70.66, copy JSON72.43 tok/s. It is not a58 tok/s ordinary-chat guarantee.27 requests repeat9 fixtures.24/27 checks pass; three failures repeat one prose response. Separate historical sessions, not simultaneous paired trials;9/27 exact envelopes match across speculation arms. Current local trial uses a different engine/drafter configuration.

other_leads.why: Explicit one-Spark abliterated SGLang recipe, HashK R4 compresses PLE from51.2GB to12.8GB;6/6 smoke including22,931-token retrieval.
other_leads.limits: HashK is lossy; PLE-off alternative untested. Configured200K is not usable allocation: successful receipt allocated32,896 KV tokens. Text only, upstream output corruption after traffic acknowledged, sustained/concurrent reliability unqualified. Lower priority than recipes preserving PLE with disk backing.

decision: The three additional one-Spark trials are complete. T3 is the strongest additional candidate for further qualification in this sample; EXL3 is fastest but fails the workspace-tool coding task and claims an unperformed edit. LR7 also fails that tool task. No live switch or final model selection.
